ops.title: F1 trigger space: the credential observation layer absorbs read failures; only the config boundary strands
ops.body:
Established during F1 (stranded-row recovery, fixed in 4b3eadf + 648d508) by two failed fault injections, then confirmed by probe.

**The fact.** A failing keychain `Read` cannot strand credential recovery: `creds.ClassifyRead` buckets any unrecognized error as `ReadFatal`, and `credentialObservationAt` renders that as an *observed slot state* rather than returning an error — the observation layer is deliberately absorbent. The only in-the-wild path that fails `recoverRetiredCredentialOperation` post-takeover (the strand window) is the config-boundary validation erroring *before* any read: `credentialStore` → `validateStoredCredentialBoundary` → `credentialPublicPath`/`ValidateAccountConfigDir`, e.g. the stable execution symlink under `~/.cc-pool/config/<instance>` missing (`validate account credential execution link: lstat ...`).

**Why it matters.** (1) It bounds F1's blast radius: the admission fence protects a narrow, environmental seam — filesystem damage to the account's execution-link layout — not keychain flakiness. (2) It rules out the absorbent read path as a second instance of the defect class. (3) Anyone injecting faults into recovery should target the boundary validation, not `creds.Store.Read`; the read path was probed twice and absorbed both injections (an unclassifiable error and a removed plain config dir — the latter never reaches validation because admitted accounts' real ConfigDir is the stable symlink, not the caller-supplied path).

**Strand window, precisely** (also in 648d508's commit body): the account-identity re-check runs pre-takeover, so `ErrAccountGenerationChanged`/`GetAccount` failures leave the row foreign and re-presentable; only post-takeover settle failures strand; the pending-adds leg never strands — a failed retirement retains the foreign-owned reservation.

Regression pin: `TestStrandedCredentialRecoveryFencesAdmissionAndRetries` (internal/pool/credential_operation_recovery_test.go) uses the boundary trigger — symlink removed, fence proven, symlink restored, retry commits and the account admits new work.
